tldr: Local causal heterogeneity can be smoother than the confounding regressions. When cheap records retain true outcomes but weaken treatment labels, outcome information and treatment-linked information need not buy the same precision. The sole novelty kernel is the complete absolute-risk point-CATE frontier over the fixed full-Uniform parent with the stipulated propensity, marginal-outcome and effect smoothness. A bounded finite original-record estimator and a matching all-estimator converse are required together. The supplied-propensity theorem provides a same-parent benchmark, and its exact order-recovery comparison is a corollary of the frontier. The uniform design, moderate-effect cap and armwise probability interiors are deliberate restrictions for a prospective planning model; an affine binary-response family verifies nonemptiness. The rate and the role of the two information coordinates are derived outputs. The result has technical subfield ambition; conditional-effect identification under misclassification, IV heterogeneity bounds and regular mean-effect efficiency receive prior-art credit.
gap: Conditional effects under treatment misclassification already appear in Mahajan (2006) and Lewbel (2007); Ura (2018) establishes sharp complier-effect bounds and uniform inference with endogenous treatment. The matched supervised point-CATE theorem concerns a different observed channel, and external-validation ATE efficiency addresses a mean effect. The unresolved object here is the stipulated known-symmetric-channel mixed-source point-CATE minimax risk, including a converse on the fixed full-Uniform parent. These different published targets and criteria do not establish a general non-reducibility result.
